name: Mycophenolate mofetil
route_note: oral tablets, capsules or suspension twice daily; IV infusion
originator: Syntex (Anthony Allison and Elsie Eugui); now Roche

discovery.note: Mycophenolic acid was isolated from Penicillium as one of the first antibiotics; Syntex later made the morpholinoethyl ester prodrug to improve bioavailability.

tagline: Prodrug of mycophenolic acid that selectively starves lymphocytes of guanine
summary: Mycophenolate mofetil is a prodrug of mycophenolic acid, which inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase and depletes guanosine nucleotides in lymphocytes. It is a standard part of immunosuppression after kidney, heart and liver transplantation and is widely used for lupus nephritis and other autoimmune diseases. It is strongly teratogenic.
mechanism: Mycophenolic acid is a reversible, non-competitive inhibitor of IMPDH, the rate-limiting enzyme in de novo synthesis of guanosine nucleotides, with greater potency against the type II isoform expressed in activated lymphocytes.
T and B lymphocytes depend heavily on the de novo pathway, whereas other cells can use the salvage pathway, so lymphocyte proliferation and antibody formation are selectively suppressed.
uses: Prophylaxis of rejection in kidney, heart and liver transplantation
Lupus nephritis (widely used; labelled in some countries)
Other autoimmune diseases such as vasculitis and myasthenia gravis (off-label)

history.title: Mycophenolic acid
history.detail: Bartolomeo Gosio isolates mycophenolic acid from Penicillium mould.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: CellCept approved for prevention of kidney transplant rejection, replacing azathioprine in many regimens.

history.title: ALMS trial
history.detail: Mycophenolate is shown to be comparable to IV cyclophosphamide for lupus nephritis induction.

history.title: REMS
history.detail: FDA approves a mycophenolate REMS focused on pregnancy prevention.

pk.metabolism: hydrolysis to MPA; glucuronidation to inactive MPAG with enterohepatic recycling

serious: serious infections including PML and CMV
safety.boxed_warning: Embryofetal toxicity (first-trimester pregnancy loss and congenital malformations), malignancies such as lymphoma, and serious infections.

facts: An enteric-coated salt, mycophenolate sodium (Myfortic, Novartis), was approved in the US in 2004.
Because of embryofetal toxicity, US prescribing has been governed by a single mycophenolate REMS programme since 2012.
